title: Valence Systems Implementation Launch & Security Onboarding
summary: Kickoff for Valence Systems' Redwood Private deployment. Main focus: align timeline for staging->pilot->prod, confirm SecOps requirements (KMS/HSM, audit logs), finalize network handoff (VPC peering vs transit), and schedule an on-prem dry run for the quantized model bundle. Action items assigned for runbook edits, security doc exchange, and a performance smoke test in their staging environment.
action_items: Diego Marin: Share onboarding runbook draft and staging checklist (due 2026-11-04)
Arjun Patel: Provide recommended quantization profile and perf knobs for their 8xA100 footprint (due 2026-11-06)
Priya Kapoor (Valence): Send SOC2 scope doc and KMS requirements to Redwood security (due 2026-11-03)
Jamal Reed (Valence): Provision a staging VPC and invite Redwood IPs for smoke tests (due 2026-11-05)
next_steps: Redwood to upload onboarding-runbook link and security packet: https://redwood.example.com/runbooks/valence
Schedule 2-hour staging smoke test window the week of 2026-11-08
Arjun to run synthetic perf test on customer sample prompts and share token/latency breakdown
header:
Date: 2026-11-01
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 54 mins
Location: Zoom
Recording: yes
Attendees: Olivia Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Marin (Redwood CSM), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE); Tara Nguyen (Valence), Marcus Holt (Valence CTO), Priya Kapoor (Valence SecOps), Jamal Reed (Valence Platform), Ana Ruiz (Valence PM)
transcript:
00:00:00 - Olivia: Hey everyone, uh thanks for carving out time. Olivia from Redwood, I'll run the agenda quick. Diego and Arjun are with me.
00:00:12 - Tara: Thanks. Super excited. we're, um, ready to kick off, there's a lot wrapped into this migration so, appreciate the alignment.
00:00:25 - Diego: Quick agenda — timeline, security checklist, VPC options, runbook handoffs, and pos— pilot success metrics, plus Q&A.
00:00:38 - Marcus: Sounds good. Our priority is data residency and auditability. We need proof that logs and KMS calls are captured for our auditors.
00:00:50 - Priya: Yeah and also HSM support — we can't rely on customer-managed keys only; we need integration with our on-prem HSM for key wraps.
00:01:03 - Arjun: Okay, good — so Redwood Private supports both KMS and HSM flows. small caveat: the initial package we ship uses a KMS shim for cloud KMS, but we have a documented HSM connector path. we'll include the HSM integration playbook.
00:01:22 - Jamal: When you say shim — is that gonna impact first-byte latency? We're sensitive to tail p99 for the agent flows.
00:01:30 - Arjun: Good question. For HSM wraps there's a negligible extra ms per session establishment, it's mostly amortized. the serving runtime and KV cache remain local so token latency isn't materially different once sessions are established. I can share measured numbers from a previous on-prem test.
00:01:48 - Olivia: We'll attach a perf spreadsheet. It has token-level breakdowns for models and sequence lengths.
00:01:55 - Tara: Great. On network — we prefer VPC peering to avoid NAT traversal. Does Redwood support both peering and transit via a customer egress firewall?
00:02:06 - Diego: We support VPC peering and secured transit. For customers with strict ingress rules we recommend peering; for multi-region corporate networks transit with IP allowlist is common. We'll document the IP ranges.
00:02:22 - Marcus: Do you have an approval template for peering and a runbook for creating routes? Our network team will want cut-and-pasteable steps.
00:02:31 - Arjun: Yep. there's a step-by-step runbook and terraform snippets. I'll send those. expect a staging checklist that includes routes, security groups, and a smoke test plan.
00:02:45 - Olivia: Let's anchor the timeline — customer wants a pilot by the end of November. We're looking at three phases: staging (this week), pilot (2 weeks), and production rollout. Is that feasible given your teams?
00:02:58 - Tara: tight but possible. internal approval for pilot is scheduled 11/09. so pilot start 11/10 would be ideal.
00:03:08 - Diego: Works on our side, we'd aim to do staging smoke test 11/08 or 11/09.
00:03:14 - Jamal: We need a dry run in our on-prem lab first though — can we do a local bundle test before we open the VPC?
00:03:21 - Arjun: Absolutely. we can provide a quantized model bundle and a local runtime container. That lets you validate inference and quantization footprint without network.
00:03:34 - Priya: What's in the bundle? Does it include telemetry hooks? we need to be sure it's not phoning home except to approved endpoints.
00:03:42 - Arjun: The bundle includes the model artifacts, runtime binary, and a telemetry toggle. by default telemetry is disabled for air-gapped runs; when enabled it only emits to configured endpoints. We'll provide a telemetry config doc.
00:03:56 - Marcus: Can you support side-by-side canary routing? we might want to route 10% traffic to Redwood Dedicated first.
00:04:04 - Diego: For Private that pattern still works — the control plane can route by policy. for Strict air-gapped infra we mimic canary behavior with traffic split rules.
00:04:15 - Ana: a small question — cost reporting: will we see token-level cost in the console for private clusters?
00:04:23 - Olivia: Yes, you'll get per-route token accounting in Redwood Console. For Private deployments we ship an agent that aggregates usage and sends billing rollups to your billing account. detailed token logs can be kept locally if required.
00:04:38 - Tara: Good. ok security specifics. Priya, can you run through the SOC2 items we need Redwood to provide?
00:04:45 - Priya: Sure. We need: A) SOC2 Type II scoped report or an equivalent control statement; B) Audit logs retention, searchability; C) SSO integration with our IdP (SAML/SCIM for provisioning); D) Encryption-in-transit and at-rest proof; E) KMS/HSM attestations. do you have a SOC2 cert?
00:05:05 - Diego: Redwood has SOC2 Type II and ISO attestation. we'll share the cert and a controls matrix. audit logs are configurable to forward to your SIEM via syslog or S3 exports. SAML and SCIM supported.
00:05:18 - Priya: For audit logs retention — we need 5 years for certain logs. is that possible?
00:05:24 - Olivia: For Private deployments you can control retention. we'll show options: local retention + optional archived exports to a secure S3 with lifecycle policies.
00:05:34 - Tara: Excellent. can you confirm RBAC granularity? our teams want token-scoped roles per environment.
00:05:42 - Arjun: You can map IdP groups to RBAC roles, and we support environment-scoped roles (staging/pilot/prod) and token-scoped access. We'll include sample policies.
00:05:54 - Marcus: Back to perf — Arjun, can you outline the perf test you'll run? sample prompts, concurrency, and expected p95 for 512 tokens?
00:06:03 - Arjun: I'll run synthetic tests with the customer's sample prompt set at concurrency 8 and token length 512. Expect p95 around 120-160ms per token on your 8xA100 config with a continuous batch of 8; I'll share exact numbers.
00:06:16 - Jamal: And regression alerts — can Redwood watch prompt sets and alert if quality drops after model swaps?
00:06:22 - Diego: Redwood Optimize includes quality-monitoring tied to prompt sets and evals. We can configure regression thresholds and auto-rollback for production routes.
00:06:34 - Tara: Good. Next, who will be the single point of contact for the pilot?
00:06:40 - Ana: I'm going to be PM for the rollout and will coordinate.
00:06:44 - Olivia: Great, Ana will be the internal valence PM contact. Diego will be CSM primary on Redwood side. Arjun will lead technical tasks.
00:06:54 - Diego: I'll set up a shared Jira board and invite all the owners.
00:06:58 - Marcus: Any known blockers we should be aware of from previous customers?
00:07:03 - Arjun: Typical blockers are network egress rules and KMS approval cycles. The HSM connector sometimes requires an extra iteration with SecOps, but the playbook short-circuits most of that.
00:07:17 - Priya: we may need a brief architecture review with your security engineer — can we schedule 30-45 minutes for that?
00:07:23 - Olivia: Yes, we'll schedule a security deep-dive next week.
00:07:27 - Diego: Action items: we'll circulate the runbook, send SOC2/ISO artifacts, and Arjun will deliver quantization profile.
00:07:36 - Tara: Perfect. One last item — data retention for embeddings. We will not allow long-term storage of derived vectors unless encrypted at rest with our key.
00:07:45 - Arjun: By default embeddings can be configured to be ephemeral; for any persisted vectors we support customer-managed encryption and an expiration policy. We'll include that config example.
00:07:58 - Olivia: Okay wrapping — recap of next steps: Diego runbook, Arjun perf + quant profile, Valence to provision staging VPC and send SOC2 scope.
00:08:12 - Ana: I'll coordinate scheduling with Jamal and Priya for the staging window.
00:08:18 - Olivia: Awesome — we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs package. Thanks everyone.
00:08:24 - Marcus: Thanks.
00:08:26 - (meeting continues with sidebar technical clarifications and crosstalk; notes truncated to main thread)
00:40:15 - Arjun: sharing terraform snippets here, note— you need route tables updated before peer acceptance to avoid blackhole.
00:42:05 - Jamal: got it. we'll also test with iperf to validate throughput.
00:49:32 - Diego: ok final note — we'll set up a shared slack channel for real-time smoke test support.
00:53:50 - Olivia: End of recording, thanks everyone.
